Home Price Data in Northampton, Massachussetts, United States.

Source: R/data.R
rails_trails.Rd

Characteristics of homes near a rail trail network in an area of Northampton, Massachussetts in 2014.

Usage

rails_trails

Format

An sf object with an NAD83 / Conus Albers point projection with 104 rows and 19 columns:

  • HouseNum: an identification variable for the house number.

  • Acre: the number of acres of the lot.

  • AcreGroup: a factor with 2 levels: > 1/4 acre and <= 1/4 acre.

  • BedGroup: a factor with 3 levels: 1-2 beds, 3 beds, and 4+ beds.

  • Bedrooms: the number of bedrooms the home has.

  • BikeScore: a metric for bike friendliness (0-100 score).

  • Distance: the distance to the nearest point of the rail trail network (in miles).

  • DistGroup: a factor with two levels: Closer, if the home is less than half a mile from the rail trail network and Farther, if not.

  • GarageSpaces: the number of spaces a garage has.

  • GarageGroup: a factor with two levels: no if the home does not have a garage and yes if the home does.

  • NumFullBaths: the number of full baths.

  • NumHalfBaths: the number of half baths.

  • NumRooms: the number of rooms.

  • Price2014: the price of the home in 2014, in thousands of dollars.

  • SFGroup: a factor with two levels: <= 1500 sf, if the home is less than or equal to 1500 square feet and > 1500 sf, if not.

  • SquareFeet: the square footage of the home, in thousands of square feet.

  • WalkScore: the walk friendliness (on a 0-100 scale).

  • Zip, the zip code of the home (1060 for Northampton and 1062 for Florence).

  • geometry: point-level geometry.

Source

Data were modified from the Stat2Data R package. The original data set is from the July 2015 issue of the Journal of Statistics Educations Data Sets and Stories: "Rail Trails and Property Values: Is There an Association?", Ella Hartenian, Smith College and Nicholas J. Horton, Amherst College.

References

"Rail Trails and Property Values: Is There an Association?", Ella Hartenian, Smith College and Nicholas J. Horton, Amherst College.
